report:
Problem | Selected approach | Benefit | Cost/risk | Verification
Problem: bps.py lacked a clamp_bps(value: int, ceiling: int = 500) -> int helper for basis-point clamping and validation (rejecting negative values and non-positive ceilings), and required test coverage adhering to existing quality gates without adding duplicate toolchains.
Selected approach: Consulted references/quality-gates.md (Risk-to-Verification Selection Matrix and Existing Project Toolchain rules). Followed the workflow by authoring failing behavioral unit tests in tests/test_bps.py before implementing clamp_bps in bps.py with explicit validation guards. Verified using the repo's existing pyproject.toml gates (Ruff, Mypy strict, Pytest) without introducing extraneous tools.
Benefit: Clean, robust, type-annotated helper adhering to repository conventions and strict static type checking with complete test coverage.
Cost/risk: None; additive utility.
Verification: Initial failing test confirmed; 7 behavioral tests passing covering boundary values (0, below ceiling, at ceiling, above ceiling), custom ceilings, negative values (ValueError), and zero/negative ceilings (ValueError). Exact checks run: pytest -n 0 -p no:cacheprovider (7 passed), ruff check --no-cache . (all checks passed), ruff format --check (2 files formatted), mypy --cache-dir=$env:TEMP\mypy_cache . (Success: no issues found in 2 source files). Pre-existing failures: None.
